ms_boulder_garden.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone boulders tucked into the hardwood and pine forest just inside Tishomingo State Park, beside a quiet stream. The problems stay low to moderate in height, topping out around fifteen feet, with a mix of faces, cracks, slabs, arêtes and a few overhanging roofs. The grades lean easy: most problems fall between VB and V3, with only a couple of harder lines, so it suits beginners, families and anyone warming up. Tree cover keeps the rocks shaded for much of the day, which helps in warm weather. Bring a pad and a spotter for the taller problems.
ms_boulder_garden.parking_note: Use the little pullout beside the ranger station near the park entrance. The boulders sit a short way off, close to the stream.
ms_boulder_garden.approach: A marked footpath begins across the road from the parking area and reaches the boulders in roughly a hundred yards.

mt_bad_rock_canyon.blurb: A roadside bouldering spot along the highway between Columbia Falls and Hungry Horse, also known locally as Berne Park. Most problems are short, ten to fourteen feet, with flat landings, sit starts and crimpy or mantle-style finishes. The holds can be sharp and a few edges are brittle, so brush and inspect before pulling hard. Grades run mostly from V0 to V4 with a handful of harder lines, plus a few roped routes. The walk from the pullout is only a few minutes. Spring and fall are the favored seasons, and in summer early or evening sessions are cooler. Bring two pads and a spotter.
mt_bad_rock_canyon.parking_note: Pull into the wide gravel turnout beside the highway; the problems start just above it.
mt_bad_rock_canyon.approach: A short scramble up from the turnout, usually under ten minutes and often much less.

mt_winter_wall.blurb: A roadside gneiss wall above the Madison River near Norris, known as one of the sunnier, drier places to climb around Bozeman when snow still lingers at higher crags. The folded rock holds a mix of bolted sport lines and trad routes, including a few multi-pitch climbs high above the river. Grades range from the 5.7s to the low 5.12s, with the bulk of routes in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so it works for a variety of abilities. The approach is short but brushy with some loose rock, so scout your line and watch for stones from parties above. Expect wind at times.
mt_winter_wall.parking_note: Two small pullouts on the river side of the highway sit close below the wall, roughly a mile beyond the Bear Trap bridge. A boat launch down the road offers a longer walk-up alternative.
mt_winter_wall.approach: A brief, brushy scramble from the pullouts, with loose footing in places.

mt_hold_up_bluffs_north.blurb: The most visited crag at Stone Hill, sitting right beside Highway 37 above Lake Koocanusa. The rock is very hard quartzite with sharp edges, thin cracks and steep slabs, so the climbing is mostly face and edging with some crack moves. Routes mix bolts and traditional gear, with a majority of trad lines and a good number of sport routes. Grades start around 5.5 and run into the 5.12s, with the densest cluster in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. A pit toilet is on site and the approach is brief, so it is easy to fit in a half day. Walk-off descents are common.
mt_hold_up_bluffs_north.approach: Almost no hike; the base of the cliffs is a few steps from the road.

mt_hantavirus_cave.blurb: A steep, overhanging cave in the Storm Castle area of Gallatin Canyon, home to some of the hardest and most sustained climbing near Bozeman. Nearly all routes are bolted sport lines, and the grades start around 5.10 and climb well into the 5.12s and low 5.13s, so most of the climbing is for strong leaders. Expect powerful, pumpy movement on steep rock, and a compression test piece just right of the cave draws attention. The trail is short but climbs steadily up a drainage. Parking is limited to a couple of small pullouts, so share rides when you can.
mt_hantavirus_cave.parking_note: Cross the old bridge heading toward Storm Castle, take the right fork, and drive a little under a mile to a pair of small pullouts.
mt_hantavirus_cave.approach: A short, well-worn trail goes straight up a gully, with a few small switchbacks near the end.

mt_skyline_south.blurb: The southern side of Skyline Buttress on the east side of Gallatin Canyon, a gneiss tower with technical trad and some sport climbing. The faces here point south and southwest, so they warm up earlier than the cool north side, and an early start beats the heat on hot days. Climbs follow cracks, grooves, chimneys and stems, with some easy scrambling, and the character is closer to alpine than to roadside cragging, so bring extra layers and gear. Grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, centered around 5.11. The hike in is a steady one, around forty minutes from the river.
mt_skyline_south.approach: Follow the river a bit under half a mile, then head uphill into the woods and take the right-hand branch at the fork toward the buttress.

mt_genesis_area.blurb: A cluster of waterfall ice and mixed lines in Hyalite Canyon, within a short hike of the Grotto Falls trailhead. The routes include popular moderate flows around WI3 to WI4, a few steeper WI5 pitches, and mixed climbs from M4 to M8. Some of the ice pours over a rock band, and the longer links can turn into full multi-pitch days. Early in the season, lower flows can be thin and wet, so look at how much ice has formed. The approach involves sidehilling and talus to reach the upper flows. Reliable ice generally forms in winter, from around December into March.
mt_genesis_area.approach: About fifteen minutes from the trailhead lot to the first flows, with steeper sidehilling through trees and talus to the upper ones.

nv_clear_light_cave.blurb: A huge limestone cavern on the east side of Mount Potosi, about an hour from Las Vegas, and one of the steepest sport climbing venues in the country. Every route is bolted and hard, with grades concentrated at 5.12 and 5.13 and a few higher, so this is a place for strong, experienced leaders. Expect overhanging, gymnastic, pumpy climbing. The cave stays out of view during most of the hike, which ends with a steep, loose trail. The walls see a mix of sun and shade through the day, and winter and shoulder months are more comfortable than midsummer heat.
nv_clear_light_cave.approach: Follow the road west from the lot until it drops into a wash, continue up the wash, then take a steep, loose path to the cave. Allow 40 to 50 minutes.
